decisive_items: weakness of the distal phalanx of the thumb and middle phalanx of the index finger
electromyographic evaluation of the left upper limb showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve
inability to perform the “Ok” sign and to form a fist
response.rationale: R2 directly matches the raw EMG finding of neurogenic atrophy in anterior interosseous nerve-innervated muscles and the classic Ok-sign/fist weakness, which is pathognomonic. C1 adds only the left upper limb localization already present in the vignette, so it is a weaker completion. R3 and R5 lack specific raw support for AIN distribution and introduce unsupported mechanisms.

rejected.why: No raw evidence of multiple mononeuropathies; EMG shows single nerve territory, and no sensory or systemic findings.
Sudden weakness and EMG changes are nonspecific; no pain or shoulder-girdle involvement typical of neuralgic amyotrophy, and AIN-specific muscles are highlighted.
